No, not all prime numbers are even. Prime numbers greater than 2 are always odd.

To explain why:
- A prime number is defined as a natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.
- If we consider any prime number \( p \) greater than 2, it can be written in the form \( p = 2k + 1 \), where \( k \) is an integer. This is because:
  - Any even number (like 2, 4, 6, ...) can be divided by 2.
  - So if \( p \) were even, it would have a divisor of 2 other than 1 and itself.

Therefore, any prime number greater than 2 must be odd.
